$comment: Everything falls through to index.html for client-side routing, EXCEPT real
files that must be served as themselves.
sw.js is the one that bites: a service worker rewritten to index.html is
served as HTML, the browser refuses to register a script with the wrong MIME
type, and browser notifications fail in production while working perfectly in
development — where Vite serves the file directly and no rewrite exists.
A service worker is also only allowed to control the scope it is served
from, which is another reason it must stay at the root rather than move

headers.$comment: Lets the worker control the whole origin, not just /.
